text.content: Sofia now knows both patterns — sequential when each step depends on the one before, parallel when independent agents can work at the same time. But real Cascadia requests do not label themselves. A support message about a delayed shipment might work better sequentially (verify order → check shipping → generate reply) or in parallel (check shipping AND check warranty AND check account status, all at once, then merge). Which pattern to choose is one of the highest-leverage decisions in a multi-agent design, and getting it wrong costs latency or coordination overhead that never had to exist.

Summary

text.content: Choosing between sequential and parallel orchestration is less about technology and more about dependencies. Sequential orchestration works best when each step requires information from the previous step. Parallel orchestration works best when multiple agents can investigate different aspects of a problem independently.

rich_text.plain_text: Choosing between sequential and parallel orchestration is less about technology and more about dependencies. Sequential orchestration works best when each step requires information from the previous step. Parallel orchestration works best when multiple agents can investigate different aspects of a problem independently.

text.content: The most effective multi-agent systems often combine both approaches: parallel branches handle independent work, while sequential stages coordinate decisions and assemble the final result. This ability to match the orchestration pattern to the business problem is a key part of designing reliable agent systems.
